I have a cat named Milo.
He is usually a calm cat and likes to sleep most of the day.
He almost never tries to go outside at all.
Last Tuesday, I opened the front door to bring in a package.
Milo was sitting nearby, and I didn't think much about it at the time.
I picked up the package and closed the door behind me.
A few hours later, I looked for Milo to feed him his dinner.
I checked his favorite spots around the apartment, but he wasn't there.
I called his name softly, but he didn't come to me.
I searched the whole apartment, room by room, very carefully.
I looked under the bed, behind the couch, and inside the closet.
Milo was nowhere to be found anywhere in the apartment.
Then I remembered the open door from earlier that day.
I felt a cold, worried feeling in my stomach right away.
Milo must have slipped outside without me even noticing him.
I went outside and called his name loudly, over and over.
A few neighbors looked out their windows, but no one had seen a cat.
I walked around the building twice, but I found absolutely nothing.
It started to get dark, and I felt more and more worried by the minute.
I made a small sign with Milo's picture and put it near the entrance.
I hoped that someone passing by would see it.
That night, I could barely sleep at all.
I kept thinking about where Milo might be right now.
Was he scared?
Was he hungry, cold, or lost somewhere nearby?
I checked outside my window three or four times.
The next morning, I heard a soft sound outside my door, very early.
I opened it quickly, and there was Milo, sitting calmly like nothing had happened.
He looked a little dirty but seemed completely fine otherwise.
I picked him up and held him for a long time in my arms.
I felt so relieved that I almost cried a little bit.
He just looked at me like he didn't understand why I was so upset, and then he simply fell asleep on my shoulder.
Now, I check twice before opening the front door, every single time.
Milo taught me that even a calm cat can surprise you sometimes.
One missing day felt like the longest day of my entire year, and I never want to feel that scared again.
